title: feat(plugin-auth): an OAuth consent binds the consenting session's active organization, carried as organization_id
body:
Fixes #24166

Clause-②: yes (widening)

Slice 2 of #24137 (ruling `6232069920`, letter A, the maintainer's 「同意」). #24137 keeps the runtime read and its pins; nothing in this PR reads the claim at the MCP door, and nothing in `packages/runtime` or `packages/core` changes. Upstream slice #24165 landed the contract member (`b1845ed637`).

## What changed

- **`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts`, the `oauthProvider({ … })` options.** Two seams the installed provider declares:
  - `postLogin.consentReferenceId` answers the consenting session's `activeOrganizationId` (better-auth's field on the session of record), or `undefined` when it has none. It reads the session the provider hands it and nothing else. `postLogin` is one declared object, so its other two members ride along: `shouldRedirect: () => false` (no extra selection page; the organization is the one the session already has) and `page` (read only when `shouldRedirect` answers true, which it never does; it names the consent page).
  - `customAccessTokenClaims` emits the consent's reference as `organization_id`, and nothing when there is none.
- **`verifyMcpAccessToken`.** Its own return type gains `organizationId?: string`, matching `IAuthService`'s, and it returns the `organization_id` claim there. A token whose `organization_id` is present but is not a non-empty string is refused (`null`), the method's fail-closed posture for any token this server does not mint. The `client_credentials` refusal and the JWKS cache region are untouched.
- **`packages/platform-objects`.** The `reference_id` description on `sys_oauth_consent`, `sys_oauth_refresh_token` and `sys_oauth_access_token` names the bound organization. The `en` bundle rows were regenerated with `pnpm i18n:extract`. The three translated values per locale (zh-CN, ja-JP, es-ES) were re-translated by hand, which the AGENTS.md documentation-guardrails row allows for translated-locale values; the generator then kept them. `sys_oauth_application.reference_id` is unchanged: the provider writes it only from `clientReference`, an option plugin-auth does not pass (measured below).
- `auth-schema-config.ts`: the `oauthConsent` mapping's doc comment said the column was "for client-supplied correlation", which this change makes false. Comment only.
- One changeset: `@objectstack/plugin-auth` minor, `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch.

## Premises, measured on the installed `@better-auth/oauth-provider@1.7.3` (the lockfile pin)

Paths are under `node_modules/@better-auth/oauth-provider/dist/`.

1. **The seams exist and compose.**
   - Declared: `oauth-1Ud-hvZY.d.mts:1540-1574` (`postLogin { page; consentReferenceId({ user, session, scopes }); shouldRedirect }`), `:1698-1704` (`customAccessTokenClaims({ user, referenceId, scopes, resources, metadata })`).
   - Consent row: the consent endpoint calls `consentReferenceId` and creates the row with that `referenceId` (`authorize-9whjxVLJ.mjs:67-118`).
   - Code: `/oauth2/authorize` calls it again and puts it on the authorization code (`:5646-5700`; `redirectWithAuthorizationCode` at `:5706-5733` stores it).
   - Mint: the code exchange passes `verificationValue.referenceId` (`introspect-CbhhXT0E.mjs:2040`), the refresh row stores it (`:1545-1556`), a refresh passes `refreshToken.referenceId` (`:2177`), and `resolveAccessTokenClaims` hands it to `customAccessTokenClaims` on both paths (`:239-262`).
   - `organization_id` is not in `RESERVED_ACCESS_TOKEN_CLAIMS` (`:189-202`), so it is not stripped. Read off the minted token below.
2. **The session's value, never the client's.** The hook's context is `{ user, session, scopes }` only; the authorize query, the consent body and the client metadata never reach it. Pinned with a real organization the user belongs to passed as `organization_id`, `organizationId`, `reference_id` and `referenceId` on the authorize request: the consent row, the refresh row and the token all carry the session's organization.
3. **Existing consents re-confirm once.** The provider's own seam: `/oauth2/authorize` adds `referenceId` to the consent lookup whenever the hook answers one (`authorize-9whjxVLJ.mjs:5660-5676`), so a consent with a null reference no longer matches and the user is sent to the consent page (`:5677-5680`). Nothing extra was wired. Pinned as a differential: the same stored consent is honoured with no organization in play (control), re-prompts once an organization is active, and is not prompted a second time after re-confirming. An old refresh family keeps minting tokens with no claim.
4. **A record, not an authorization.** This PR records and returns the organization only. Notes for the runtime read are in the acceptance notes.

## Clause-② measurement (built entry declarations, BASE `a237d7f496` vs this branch)

- `@objectstack/plugin-auth` `dist/index.d.ts` and `dist/index.d.mts`: the one declaration change is in `verifyMcpAccessToken(token: string)`: its resolved object type gains `organizationId?: string;` beside `userId`, `scopes` and `clientId?` (head line 3222, inside the declaration at head lines 3218-3223; BASE lines 3208-3212). The rest of the diff is doc-comment prose (the method's docblock, and the `AUTH_OAUTH_CONSENT_SCHEMA` comment).
- `@objectstack/platform-objects` `dist/index.d.ts`, `index.d.mts`, `plugin.d.ts`, `plugin.d.mts`: byte-identical (`diff` exit 0; md5 equal).

## Tests

- New real-flow pin `src/auth-manager.oauth-consent-organization.test.ts`: the options a real `AuthManager` hands `oauthProvider()`, booted in a real better-auth server with the real provider and the real `organization` plugin, driven DCR, sign-up, organization, authorize, consent, token and refresh. Five cases:
  - token `organization_id` equals the session's active organization; consent row and refresh row `reference_id` equal it; `verifyMcpAccessToken` returns `organizationId`;
  - a refresh keeps the consent's organization after the session moves to another one;
  - no active organization: no reference, no claim, no `organizationId` member;
  - organization-looking authorize parameters change nothing recorded;
  - re-confirm once, plus the old refresh family staying unbound.
- `src/auth-manager.mcp-oauth.test.ts`: three claim-shape pins on the verifier (the claim is returned; no claim means no member; a present non-string or empty claim is refused, with the string case as control).
- Ablation, once, through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (the test imports `./auth-manager` source, so no `dist` leg): `consentReferenceId` replaced by `() => undefined`, anchor 1 to 0, blob `ab0876f238ad` to `8422b44fd87d`. Result: 4 failed, 1 passed (the no-organization case, which asserts absence and is expected to stay green). Restore: blob equals HEAD (`ab0876f238ad`) and `git diff HEAD` empty.
- Measured on head `81b7b99c2` (the final commit), all under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` (shared-box seconds).
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth typecheck`, then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-auth exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: `check:test-typecheck: OK`; `Test Files 157 passed (157)`, `Tests 3084 passed | 10 skipped (3094)`; `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
  - `pnpm --filter @objectstack/platform-objects typecheck`, then its `vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --passWithNoTests`: `check:test-typecheck: OK`; `Test Files 73 passed (73)`, `Tests 1136 passed (1136)`; `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
  - The new pin alone, verbose, at `1371aa7a3`: 5 of 5 passed; 1.29 s of tests in a 16.3 s file run (the rest is module import).
  - Local scope: the two packages' own tests and typecheck. Their import sites owe nothing extra: `platform-objects`' built declarations are byte-identical, and `plugin-auth`'s public face changes by one optional member on one return type. `test:repo` is not run locally (CI's `Test Core`); the `integration`-tier rule is `packages/cli`'s and does not apply.

## Patch round 1 (seat record `6239991736`)

- Two sentences now say what the `IAuthService.verifyMcpAccessToken` contract says, and no more: the caller vets the organization on every request by the rule that vets a session's active organization (`vetOrganizationClaim`, `@objectstack/core`). They are the changeset's last sentence under `AuthManager.verifyMcpAccessToken`, and the matching sentence in `verifyMcpAccessToken`'s docblock (commit `099568c28`). Neither restates a membership guarantee, because that rule reads no membership under `single` or with no posture (see the acceptance notes). Nothing else changed: the changeset keeps `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth` minor and `@objectstack/platform-objects` patch.
- `origin/main` merged twice (`a0f3c8304`, `1e4146df8`), with no generated file in either merge. The head is `1e4146df8`. `b7f29ddfe` (cli only) landed afterwards and is not merged.

  - `vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: `Test Files 157 passed (157)`, `Tests 3084 passed | 10 skipped (3094)`.
  - The pin file, verbose: 5 of 5 passed.
  - `platform-objects` `vitest run`: `Test Files 74 passed (74)`, `Tests 1139 passed (1139)`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Resource custom claims outrank this claim.** The provider's precedence is extension claims, then per-issuance claims, then `customAccessTokenClaims`, then a resource row's `customClaims` (`introspect-CbhhXT0E.mjs:229-262`). A `sys_oauth_resource.custom_claims` value carrying `organization_id` on the MCP resource row would therefore replace the consent-bound organization on every MCP token. Not filed: a configuration the runtime would honour, not one it drops. Carrier: #24137 (the runtime read), noted.
- **Membership is re-checked only under a wall.** `vetOrganizationClaim` (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts:762-770`) keeps a claim with no membership read under `single` or with no posture. That is the session arm as ruled, and #24137's runtime read reuses it. Under `single`, a former member's OAuth token keeps resolving in the bound organization, exactly as a REST session's claim does. Read-only inference. Carrier: #24137, noted.
- **The consent page URL now carries the session row id.** With `postLogin` configured, the provider adds `ba_pl` (the consenting session's `sys_session.id`, not its token) to the signed consent-page query (`authorize-9whjxVLJ.mjs:5735`, `:5753`), so `postLogin.shouldRedirect` is skipped on the way back. Observation. Carrier: none.
- **A consent made with no organization updates an organization-bound row's scopes.** When the hook answers no reference, the provider's consent lookup has no reference filter and can match an organization-bound consent for the same client and user, whose scopes and resources it then overwrites; its reference is kept (`authorize-9whjxVLJ.mjs:71-109`). It changes no binding. Provider semantics, observation. Carrier: none.
- **The console's consent page does not name the organization being bound.** The ruling's option A lists it as optional. Carrier: none.
- **Helper duplication.** The new pin carries its own copies of the harness helpers in `auth-manager.mcp-oauth-resource.test.ts`, which are module-local there. Sharing them would refactor that file. Carrier: none.
- **Main merged once before opening** (`8259ea03e`; the incoming commits touch `rest`, `service-settings` and dogfood, none of this diff's packages), then rebuilt and re-measured.

The contract review of record is the lane seat's (`TIER_DEFAULT`).

- **Seat's append:** the dev's two notes for the runtime read (a resource row's `customClaims` outranks `customAccessTokenClaims`; `vetOrganizationClaim` reads no membership under `single`) are carried to #24137 by the seat.
